name: International Typographic Style (Swiss Style)
visualIdentity: Swiss-style design built on a column grid, baseline alignment, repeated spacing, and asymmetric composition with generous negative space. It uses left-aligned sans-serif type with clear size hierarchy, black and white with restrained accents, and grid-aligned photography. The source labels it a supplemental reference, not a directly named style in its collection.
suitableUses: Explicit good fits are UI and product storytelling, editorial and minimalist layouts, and motion posters or staged geometric compositions. The source also suggests Swiss style alone for posters, identity, and typographic statements where grid and type carry everything. Other uses are inferred and unverified.
limitations: The source gives no explicit limitations for the style itself. Its combination guidance avoids script or display faces, multi-hue palettes, and decorative motion without a stated value. Animation must not disrupt reading order. Example durations, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional, and the source does not specify them for this task.
palette: Suggested black and white with one red accent: background #FFFFFF, foreground #000000, accent #D32F2F. These are authored suggestions that approved or task colors override. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background is 21:1; white on the red accent is 4.979:1, meeting the 4.5 normal-text target. Verify composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Elements move along layout axes and settle on shared alignment points without changing reading order. Source combination guidance favors linear-to-ease-out settling with no springs or overshoot, and chart motion travels only horizontally or vertically. The style specifies no interaction itself. Four optional catalog patterns apply only when their action fits the scene. Video must not depend on live scroll or drag input.
audio: No style-specific audio is specified. Source audio guidance is topic-driven and requires no music, voiceover, or fixed layer. Intentional silence is permitted, and any choice should preserve speech intelligibility and reading holds.
assetRequirements: Loaded sans-serif fonts are required, but no font family is specified. Typography uses CSS Grid, and SVG geometry must align to the baseline grid. Grid-aligned photography is referenced but not supplied. Authorized assets must be prepared before rendering, and exact copy and output parameters are unspecified.
combinations: Style-097 may add a diagram and chart layer inside the column grid, with red reserved for one highlighted value. Style-093 may add headline motion using one sans-serif family, one red element per frame, and no overshoot. Both keep black, white, and the single red accent. Hybrids are optional; Swiss style alone suits type-led pieces.
productionApproach: HTML/CSS handles typography and layout, SVG handles geometry, and GSAP drives animated properties on one paused, seekable timeline. Optional Motion and chroma.js support animation and contrast checks. HyperFrames is the default composition and export pipeline; Remotion is only a documented fallback. Verify key frames, seeks, audio sync, and the decoded video.
